decision.abstract: HLA class I typing from short reads depends on the caller, assay and reference database; voting is proposed when the best caller is unknown. We evaluated ChampHLA-Consensus, an equal-weight plurality vote over five exome and four RNA-seq callers, made primary after a fitted rule failed to outperform it on these data. In 1000 Genomes and Geuvadis subjects with one recorded 2014 reference genotype, the vote agreed with it at 143/153 exome loci (63 subjects) and 113/118 RNA-seq loci (51 subjects), one locus above the strongest caller in each assay. They differed at three exome loci and one RNA-seq locus, too few to compare. After multiplicity correction the vote exceeded HLA-HD and T1K in exome data and T1K in RNA-seq; a deployment defect affected one RNA-seq caller. All 15 vote errors, at 10 loci, fell where a re-typing of the same exomes reports the 2014 type as incorrect; laboratory typing, checked post hoc and only there, gives the vote's type at nine. With corrected values there, HLA-HD scored 118/118 and the vote 117/118 in RNA-seq. Retained loci came mainly from two populations. These development results establish neither equivalence nor clinical validity; testing on unseen subjects is incomplete.
decision.reason: Finding JP-007 of the simulated journal-panel review of 3-4 November 2026: readers could not get the main results from the abstract. The earlier rule was internal; the journal does not require it.
